source_status: approved implementation plan; requirements are not executed outcomes

requirements.requirement: Go and native readers produce identical canonical scope digests; reject extra/duplicate fields, wildcard roots, missing identities, unsupported versions and mismatched profile/source evidence before a mutable attempt.
A direct native prepare request outside the approved effects is refused even if Python/CLI validation is bypassed. Staged exact bytes cannot bypass scope or dependency blockers.
Scope A while B has independently ready install/select/deactivate/undock/uninstall actions. B's files, selection and ownership claims remain unchanged through each A replan.
A's next valid action changes ID after verified progress: exact authorized effect is allowed; changed target receipt/root/receptor/kind or extra uninstall receipt is refused.

A requires action B: full-plan prerequisite remains visible and blocks A; B is not automatically authorized. Explicit new review is required to include its effect. PR #199 retained-dependency regression remains effective.
Ownership reconciliation preserves out-of-scope and other-profile claims; no hidden stale-claim pruning, root adoption or partial-inventory substitution. Unknown shared-root evidence blocks mutation.
Scope finishes with unrelated divergence: terminal scoped result is true, global convergence is false, full applied-state evidence is unchanged. Next scope is a new exact linked operation.

Old writer/recovery client, missing critical scope extension, changed scope on retry, incompatible replacement coordinator and scope downgrade all refuse. Legacy unscoped journals retain their explicit full-profile semantics.
Two executors race for the same prepared action; profile/root/claim changes race prepare and execute. Exactly one authorized effect occurs, or both refuse safely; no lock deadlock or implicit replay.
A real disposable process holds old payload use. Inactive/undocked metadata does not permit reclamation; every owned byte remains until the covered owner releases use.

Deterministically inject start/restart at reference scan, stop completion and first delete. Closed admission prevents a new covered user; removal holds exclusion through final owned-byte verification/deletion.
All supported launch paths, including direct serve and supervisor recovery, share the fence. Older or uncontrolled launchers cannot be silently adopted as managed users.
Stale/reused PID, wrong process generation/executable, changed endpoint/descriptor, missing manager and inaccessible other-user domain yield unknown/refused, not stopped.
Controlled child detaches or escapes the promised lifetime domain. Report unsupported/uncertain and retain bytes rather than inferring quiescence from the original process group.
Kill the controller before stop, after stop and after deletion; drop an accepted owner response. Durable retirement remains closed and recovery reconciles the same attempt before any further effect.
Partial deletion, damaged rollback artifact, changed receipt/file, symlink/hardlink/root replacement and foreign ownership refuse unsafe continuation. Recovery preserves sentinels and other versions.
Two profiles or TOPS retain the same receipt. Releasing one claim does not allow deletion; complete claimed-domain release and real use release are separately required.

Request removal of the executing controller, sole recovery reader or required audit/authorization substrate. Refuse absent an exact existing out-of-place/native maintenance route; never auto-select deferred audit or purge.

Invoke a service package's removal through the generic receipt executor. It refuses unsupported dispatch or delegates to the exact native owner; retained references and pending work cannot be bypassed.
All seven Go units map to exact supported owners. Component/owner/compiled-version substitution, forged argv and unknown critical owner metadata refuse before execution.

Install SSIAG, STAV and Accordare through their actual installers in fresh isolated prefixes; independently verify owner-generated receipt, final executable bytes and native refusal behavior. No enrollment/start is inferred from package install.

Different packaging builds of one native version coexist in distinct prefixes; a different byte set cannot overwrite the same immutable path. Old exact owner can recover/uninstall only its bound installation.
qxctl/SSH/stdio raw-delivery custody never masquerades as a native receipt. Changing future launch selection leaves existing sessions unchanged; uncertain use keeps old bytes retained.

Failed next-qxctl identity/protocol probe leaves old selection intact. Successful explicit selection retains old recovery binary; configured Linux host slots/fallbacks remain under their real host owner.

Nonroot Conda install cannot provision/elevate the optional administrator. Pending attempts bind old exact binary; reviewed admin replacement preserves profile/history/audit and required recovery bytes.

Conda update/remove/cache cleanup affects carriers only; no shared inode or duplicate ownership with runtime/rollback files. Previewed and actual transaction stay within reviewed package effects or stop.

Install → stage upgrade → explicit compatible selection → rollback → qualified retirement using exact independent module versions. Incompatible target leaves selection unchanged. Removing one component never reinstalls it through a cohort marker.

Every transition preserves user knowledge, credentials, TOPS config, journals, unrelated packages and deliberately placed foreign sentinels. Same package installed for a fresh user generates no publisher-system identity.

Run applicable installed-owner/service-manager lanes on all four core profiles and selected supplements, including user/system privilege and race cases. Missing host or manager is incomplete, not a pass.

Bind final candidate bytes, recipe/source/export/toolchain, exact owner capabilities, signatures, retrieval and real two-release results. Independent reviewer checks a failure, its correction and recovery outcome.
